from 1st Ocotber 2023 to 30th November 2023\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb style=\"background-color: #ffe599;\"\u003E1\/10\/23 to 15\/10\/23 - Posted in psychiatry department\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EMy medicine posting started with Psychiatry department which is more or less a sub branch of medicine. Without this branch, medicine is incomplete.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDuring these postings I used to sit in the OP and listen to my PGs take case history. The history taking in psychiatry is quite elaborate with attention to detail.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003ESome of the cases that I have seen are -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EAnxiety disorder\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDissociative disorder\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003ESchizophrenia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDepression\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003ETobacco and alcohol dependence syndrome\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EOn my night duty I was put incharge of a patient who had dissociative disorder. He would get agitated and start making animal sounds. I learnt how to manage this case by giving drugs like lorazepam and \u0026nbsp;haloperidol.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EI helped take surveys on impact of electronic gadgets in our day to day lives and role of religion in our lives.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EI was a part of the skit group that performed on World Mental Health Day on 10th October. Through our skit we wanted to remove the taboo from mental health and help break the stigma. The theme for this year was - Mental Health is A Universal Human Right.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #cfe2f3;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E16\/10\/23 to 31\/10\/23 -Posted in peripherals\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EICU DUTY -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EMy peripherals duty started with ICU. This is where are all the critical patients are for whom utmost care is required. I was apprehensive as it is a big responsibility but with time I got the hang of it.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDuring my icu duty I was mainly responsible for hourly monitoring of the patients. Checking vitals including BP, PR, RR, temp, sugar levels and 02 saturation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EI learnt about some emergency drugs like noradrenaline, atropine,etc.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDuring this period I also learnt how to take blood sample, ABG sample, do foley’s catheterisation and ryles tube insertion.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiW-GlE-VodKpn5KBJkkAK_pAN0mmIPMixRXH2RDijStMHx48OQjC7tCZNVGqBPYViiAu6CB8E-RcD6FHl-EyP-eVYJtMJmXSU9QoR9bNlE0zMXYEdlABZakWQR_87xz5H9ai6ba9VD8t43skCGwDs4Vd0lLpALLvuMN0KRI-0-Hmt4dw_K2iGug-531HAw\/s1024\/5b7a8c76-8f03-421c-b5fb-b0721c5d30e4.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1024\" data-original-width=\"768\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiW-GlE-VodKpn5KBJkkAK_pAN0mmIPMixRXH2RDijStMHx48OQjC7tCZNVGqBPYViiAu6CB8E-RcD6FHl-EyP-eVYJtMJmXSU9QoR9bNlE0zMXYEdlABZakWQR_87xz5H9ai6ba9VD8t43skCGwDs4Vd0lLpALLvuMN0KRI-0-Hmt4dw_K2iGug-531HAw\/s320\/5b7a8c76-8f03-421c-b5fb-b0721c5d30e4.jpeg\" width=\"240\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EI also saw an intubation being done by the PGs and gave Ambu bag ventilation. At the same time we performed CPR for the patient. The CPR was a collective effort of us interns and the patient was revived and put on mechanical ventilator but eventually he succumbed to death next day morning.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EI learnt how and when certain medications are given as infusions for example lasix infusion, norad infusion and insulin infusion.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EAnother aspect that these icu duties taught me is how important it is to counsel the patient’s attendees, to guide them through the patient treatment journey. I was also very touched by how a simple reassurance can go a long way.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003ENEPHROLOGY DUTY -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EThis was indeed one of the most hectic duties but also one where I had the most learning experience. I was amazed to see how these dialysis units work. I realised how necessary dialysis is for the CKD patients and saw even may of them come on a daily basis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EOn one day , a case had come from the casuality and the man had severe grade 4 sob and generalised body selling. His creatinine levels were high which required for him to be dialysed immediately. PG sir put a central line for his femoral vein and I assisted him and did the suturing to secure the line.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI also learnt about AV fistulas\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWARD DUTY -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis mainly consisted of monitoring BP and sugar levels of unit patients and even hypertensive and diabetic patients transferred from ophthalmology department and making sure that they get timely treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearning to do USG - detection of Ascitic fluid\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
